text: In parallelogrammic figures the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and a diagonal cuts them in half.  Let $ACDB$ be a parallelogrammic figure, and $BC$ its diagonal. I say that for parallelogram $ACDB$, the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another, and the diagonal $BC$ cuts it in half.
For since $AB$ is parallel to $CD$, and the straight-line $BC$ has fallen across  them, the alternate angles $ABC$ and $BCD$ are equal to one another [Prop.~1.29].
assertion: the alternate angles ABC and BCD are equal

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the straight-line $BC$ has fallen across  them

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: alternate angles $ABC$ and $BCD$ are equal to one another

text: Again, since $AC$ is parallel to $BD$, and $BC$ has fallen across them, the alternate angles $ACB$ and $CBD$ are equal to one another [Prop.~1.29].
assertion: the alternate angles ACB and CBD are equal

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: alternate angles $ACB$ and $CBD$ are equal to one another

text: So $ABC$ and $BCD$ are two triangles having the two angles $ABC$ and $BCA$ equal to the two (angles) $BCD$ and $CBD$, respectively, and one side equal to one side---the (one) by the equal angles and common to them, (namely) $BC$.
assertion: triangles ABC and BCD have two angles equal to two angles respectively, with the common side BC

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: the two angles $ABC$ and $BCA$ equal to the two (angles) $BCD$ and $CBD$, respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: one side equal to one side---the (one) by the equal angles and common to them, (namely) $BC$

text: Thus, they will also  have the remaining sides  equal to the corresponding remaining (sides), and the remaining angle (equal) to the remaining angle [Prop.~1.26].
assertion: the remaining sides are equal to the remaining sides, and the remaining angle equal to the remaining angle

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: they will also  have the remaining sides  equal to the corresponding remaining (sides), and the remaining angle (equal) to the remaining angle

text: And since angle $ABC$ is equal to $BCD$, and $CBD$ to $ACB$, the whole (angle) $ABD$ is thus equal to the whole (angle) $ACD$.
assertion: the whole angle ABD equals the whole angle ACD

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: whole (angle) $ABD$ is thus equal to the whole (angle) $ACD$

text: And  $BAC$ was also shown  (to be) equal to $CDB$.
assertion: angle BAC was shown equal to CDB

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $BAC$ was also shown  (to be) equal to $CDB$

text: Thus, in parallelogrammic figures the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another.
assertion: in parallelograms the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: in parallelogrammic figures the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another

text: And, I also say that a diagonal cuts them in half.
assertion: (what-to-show) a diagonal cuts them in half

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: a diagonal cuts them in half

text: For since $AB$ is equal to $CD$, and $BC$ (is) common, the two (straight-lines) $AB$, $BC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $DC$, $CB$, respectively.
assertion: the two lines AB, BC are equal to the two lines DC, CB respectively

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: two (straight-lines) $AB$, $BC$ are equal to the two (straight-lines) $DC$, $CB$, respectively

text: And angle $ABC$ is equal to angle $BCD$.
Thus, the base $AC$ (is) also equal to $DB$,
and triangle $ABC$ is equal to triangle $BCD$ [Prop.~1.4].
Thus, the diagonal $BC$ cuts the parallelogram $ACDB$ in half.
assertion: the diagonal BC cuts the parallelogram ACDB in half

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: diagonal $BC$ cuts the parallelogram $ACDB$ in half

text: (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
